statements.status_notes: Upstream GHSA-89p2-f5cv-x5cg (https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/security/advisories/GHSA-89p2-f5cv-x5cg) covers atom exhaustion through OAuth 2 JWT tag scopes: extract_scopes/1 in the rabbitmq_auth_backend_oauth2 plugin converted each rabbitmq.tag scope value to an atom with rabbit_data_coercion:to_atom. It lists the RabbitMQ 3.13 to 4.2 lines as affected, names 3.13.15, 4.0.22, 4.1.11, 4.2.6 and 4.3.1 as fixed releases, and does not list the 4.4 series. In the v4.4.0 and v4.4.1 release tags of rabbitmq-server, tags_from/1 in deps/rabbitmq_auth_backend_oauth2/src/rabbit_auth_backend_oauth2.erl keeps rabbitmq.tag scope values as binaries, so token contents no longer create atoms. This package installs the GPG-verified upstream rabbitmq-server-generic-unix release. Its only published build, on amd64 and arm64, is 4.4.1-0, which ships RabbitMQ 4.4.1 (plugin directories rabbit-4.4.1 and rabbitmq_auth_backend_oauth2-4.4.1). Checked the shipped plugin in every published build on both architectures: the compiled rabbit_auth_backend_oauth2.beam imports neither rabbit_data_coercion:to_atom nor any atom-creating BIF, while the same import-table check finds rabbit_data_coercion:to_atom in 16 other modules of the same package. That build carries the fix, so the range is fixed at 4.4.1-0.
